pharmcatOutputShape:
VERIFIED against PharmCAT source on the `development` branch (github.com/PharmGKB/PharmCAT), reading the Gson `@Expose`/`@SerializedName` annotations directly. Two distinct JSON artifacts are emitted; do NOT conflate them.

=== A. PHENOTYPER JSON — `<base>.phenotype.json` ===
Source: `src/main/java/org/pharmgkb/pharmcat/phenotype/Phenotyper.java`. Top-level keys (exactly 3):
- `matcherMetadata`: object | null
- `geneReports`: SortedMap<String, GeneReport>  — FLAT, keyed by gene symbol ("CYP2C19", "CYP2D6")
- `unannotatedGeneCalls`: GeneReport[]

=== B. REPORTER JSON — `<base>.report.json` (only with -reporterJson) ===
Source: `reporter/ReportContext.java`, serialized by `reporter/format/JsonFormat.java` via `DataSerializer.GSON.toJson(reportContext)` (no custom adapters). Top-level keys:
- `title`: string | null
- `timestamp`: Date (ISO-ish string)
- `pharmcatVersion`: string
- `dataVersion`: string
- `genes`: SortedMap<String, GeneReport>  — NOTE the key is `genes` here, NOT `geneReports`
- `drugs`: SortedMap<PrescribingGuidanceSource, SortedMap<String, DrugReport>> — NESTED TWO LEVELS
- `messages`: MessageAnnotation[]
- `matcherMetadata`: object | null
- `unannotatedGeneCalls`: GeneReport[]

`drugs` outer keys are the Java enum CONSTANT NAMES (Gson default; the enum carries no @SerializedName): "CPIC_GUIDELINE" | "DPWG_GUIDELINE" | "FDA_LABEL" | "FDA_ASSOC" (from `reporter/model/PrescribingGuidanceSource.java`). Inner keys are lowercased drug names. This enum is your guideline-source discriminator — the thing your citation layer keys off.

=== GeneReport (reporter/model/result/GeneReport.java) ===
alleleDefinitionVersion: string; alleleDefinitionSource: DataSource; phenotypeVersion: string|null; geneSymbol: string; chr: string; phased: boolean; effectivelyPhased: boolean; callSource: CallSource; uncalledHaplotypes: string[]; messages: MessageAnnotation[]; relatedDrugs: DrugLink[]; sourceDiplotypes: Diplotype[]; matcherComponentHaplotypes: Diplotype[]; matcherHomozygousComponentHaplotypes: string[]; recommendationDiplotypes: Diplotype[]; variants: VariantReport[]; variantsOfInterest: VariantReport[]; hasUndocumentedVariations: boolean; treatUndocumentedVariationsAsReference: boolean.

CRITICAL for an adapter: `sourceDiplotypes` (what was actually called) and `recommendationDiplotypes` (the possibly-collapsed/lookup form used to hit the guideline table) ARE DIFFERENT ARRAYS. Display sourceDiplotypes; join recommendations on recommendationDiplotypes.
Enums: DataSource = CPIC | DPWG | CLINPGX | FDA | UNKNOWN. CallSource = NONE | MATCHER | OUTSIDE (`reporter/model/result/CallSource.java`).

=== Diplotype (reporter/model/result/Diplotype.java) ===
allele1: Haplotype|null; allele2: Haplotype|null; gene: string; matchScore: int; phenotypes: string[]; outsidePhenotype: boolean; outsidePhenotypeMismatch: string; activityScore: string|null; outsideActivityScore: boolean; outsideActivityScoreMismatch: string; variant: VariantReport; lookupKey: string[]; label: string; inferred: boolean; inferredSourceDiplotypes: Diplotype[]|null; combination: boolean; diplotypeKey: Map<string, number>.
Note `activityScore` is a STRING (e.g. "2.0"), not a number, and is null for genes CPIC does not score (CYP2C19 among them). `phenotypes` is an ARRAY — a single call can carry more than one phenotype string. `label` is the human-readable diplotype ("CYP2C19:*1/*2"). There is NO field named `observedPhenotypes` — I checked.

=== Haplotype (reporter/model/result/Haplotype.java) ===
gene: string; name: string; function: string; reference: boolean; activityValue: string|null.

=== VariantReport (reporter/model/VariantReport.java) ===
gene: string; chromosome: string; position: long; dbSnpId: string|null; call: string|null; alleles: string[]; phased: boolean; phaseSet: int|null; referenceAllele: string (deserializes legacy alias "wildtypeAllele"); hasUndocumentedVariations: boolean; warnings: string[].
MISSING-POSITION DETECTION: there is NO serialized `missing` boolean. Java `isMissing()` is `StringUtils.isBlank(m_call)` — a derived method, not exposed. Your adapter must compute missing itself as `!v.call || v.call.trim() === ""`. This is the single easiest thing to get wrong. The complementary signal is `GeneReport.uncalledHaplotypes` (star alleles that could not be ruled in/out).

=== DrugReport (reporter/model/result/DrugReport.java) ===
name: string; id: string; source: PrescribingGuidanceSource; version: string; messages: MessageAnnotation[]; variants: string[]; urls: string[]; citations: Publication[]; guidelines: GuidelineReport[].

=== GuidelineReport (reporter/model/result/GuidelineReport.java) ===
id: string; name: string; source: PrescribingGuidanceSource; version: string; url: string; annotations: AnnotationReport[].
There is NO `population` field at this level — population lives one level deeper, on AnnotationReport.

=== AnnotationReport (reporter/model/result/AnnotationReport.java) ===
implications: string[]; drugRecommendation: string; classification: string; population: string; genotypes: Genotype[]; messages: MessageAnnotation[]; highlightedVariants: string[]; dosingInformation: boolean; alternateDrugAvailable: boolean; otherPrescribingGuidance: boolean; lookupKey: Array<Record<string, unknown>>.

ANSWERING YOUR SPECIFIC QUESTION: the recommendation TEXT is `AnnotationReport.drugRecommendation`; the strength is `classification` (CPIC's Strong/Moderate/Optional); the population is `AnnotationReport.population` (e.g. "adults", "pediatrics", "general"); the guideline SOURCE is `DrugReport.source` / `GuidelineReport.source` plus the `drugs` outer map key; the citation URL is `GuidelineReport.url` and `DrugReport.urls`/`citations`.

ADAPTER PATH for "recommendation for drug X": reportJson.drugs[SOURCE][drugName].guidelines[].annotations[] -> filter by population -> read drugRecommendation + implications + classification. Provenance for your citation table = pharmcatVersion + dataVersion + GeneReport.alleleDefinitionVersion + GeneReport.phenotypeVersion + GuidelineReport.url.
dockerInvocation:
Image is `pgkb/pharmcat` (per pharmcat.clinpgx.org/using/PharmCAT-in-Docker/). The wrapper script `pharmcat_pipeline` runs preprocessor -> matcher -> phenotyper -> reporter end-to-end.

# One-shot, JSON out, all intermediates kept:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/pharmcat/data" pgkb/pharmcat \
  pharmcat_pipeline /pharmcat/data/sample.vcf \
  -o /pharmcat/data/out \
  -reporterJson

Produces in ./data/out: sample.preprocessed.vcf.bgz, sample.match.json, sample.phenotype.json, sample.report.json, sample.report.html (and sample.missing_pgx_var.vcf if positions were absent).

# Array/consumer data: force absent positions to reference (see vcfNotes for the caveat), plus CYP2D6 outside call:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/pharmcat/data" pgkb/pharmcat \
  pharmcat_pipeline /pharmcat/data/sample.vcf \
  -o /pharmcat/data/out -reporterJson \
  --missing-to-ref \
  -po /pharmcat/data/sample.outside.tsv

# Pin the version rather than :latest for a reproducible lookup table:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/data:/pharmcat/data" pgkb/pharmcat:3.0.0 pharmcat_pipeline ...

Flags I confirmed on the docs: `-reporterJson` (long form `--reporter-save-json`), `-o`/`--output-dir`, `-bf` base filename, `-del` delete intermediates (do NOT pass this — it removes .phenotype.json), `-s`/`-S` sample selection, `-cp` concurrency, `-rs` restrict guideline sources, `-matcher`/`-phenotyper`/`-reporter` to run stages individually, `-0`/`--missing-to-ref`, `--absent-to-ref`, `--unspecified-to-ref`, `-research` for research modes.
UNCERTAIN: the exact long-form spelling of `-po` (outside-call file). The docs example shows `-po patient_cyp2d6.txt` on the `java -jar pharmcat.jar` invocation; I did not find the pharmcat_pipeline long form confirmed in writing. Run `docker run --rm pgkb/pharmcat pharmcat_pipeline --help` to pin it before wiring the adapter.

For direct jar control instead of the wrapper: `java -jar pharmcat.jar -vcf sample.vcf -reporterJson -po outside.tsv` (note: the jar does NOT run the preprocessor; the pipeline script does).
vcfNotes:
=== WHAT PHARMCAT REQUIRES ===
Verified against pharmcat.clinpgx.org/using/VCF-Requirements/ and by downloading PharmCAT's own `pharmcat_positions.vcf` from the repo.

- Reference build: GRCh38 ONLY. The header in the shipped positions file reads `##contig=<ID=chr1,assembly=GRCh38.p14,species="Homo sapiens">`. PharmCAT will not and cannot lift over for you.
- Contig naming: `chr##` (chr1, chr10, chr22), not bare `1`. The preprocessor fixes this automatically.
- Minimal header: `##fileformat=VCFv4.2`, contig lines, `##FORMAT=<ID=GT,Number=1,Type=String,Description="Genotype">`, then `#CHROM POS ID REF ALT QUAL FILTER INFO FORMAT <sampleId>`. GT is the only FORMAT field actually required.
- ALL positions must be present. This is the big one: "any position not in the input VCF is assumed to be a no call." Absent != reference. The authoritative list is `pharmcat_positions.vcf` (~1,240 records covering 22 genes: ABCG2, CACNA1S, CFTR, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, DPYD, F2, F5, G6PD, IFNL3, NAT2, NUDT15, RYR1, SLCO1B1, TPMT, UGT1A1, VKORC1). You must explicitly emit 0/0 for reference, the variant GT, or ./. for no-call.
- Preprocessor (pharmcat_vcf_preprocessor) does: strips non-PGx positions; auto-downloads the GRCh38 FASTA from NIH; normalizes to left-aligned parsimonious representation; splits/joins multiallelics into PharmCAT's expected form; fixes contig naming; optional sample filtering. Outputs `<base>.preprocessed.vcf.bgz` plus `<base>.missing_pgx_var.vcf` listing what was absent. It does NOT do liftover.
- `-0/--missing-to-ref`, `--absent-to-ref`, `--unspecified-to-ref` are all flagged DANGEROUS in the docs — they silently convert absent positions to homozygous reference and will change your calls.

=== HOW 23andMe DIFFERS ===
1. Build: 23andMe raw exports are GRCh37/hg19. PharmCAT needs GRCh38. Liftover is required and is lossy/ambiguous at some positions.
2. Format: 23andMe ships a 4-column TSV (rsid, chromosome, position, genotype) with no REF/ALT and no strand-resolved alleles — genotype is reported as two bases on the plus strand of the reference. You must derive REF/ALT per position and infer GT.
3. Coverage: genotyping, not sequencing. Of the ~1,240 PharmCAT positions, a consumer chip carries a small minority. Everything else is genuinely unknown, not reference.
4. No indels/CNV: 23andMe does not report the indels PharmCAT needs (e.g. rs5030655, a CA>C deletion at chr22:42129083 defining CYP2D6*6) and cannot see copy number at all.
5. Homozygous-reference ambiguity: 23andMe emits "--" for failed calls, which is a no-call, not reference.

=== REALISTIC CONVERSION PATH ===
Honest answer: 23andMe -> PharmCAT is a demo-grade path, not a clinical one, and the prototype should label it as such.
(a) Parse the 23andMe TSV; drop "--" rows.
(b) Liftover GRCh37 -> GRCh38 (CrossMap or UCSC liftOver with the hg19ToHg38 chain), OR — better and what I would do for a fixture — skip liftover entirely by joining on rsID against `pharmcat_positions.vcf`, which already carries the GRCh38 coordinate and REF/ALT for every position PharmCAT cares about. rsID join avoids the liftover ambiguity class of bugs.
(c) Emit GT by comparing the 23andMe base pair to the positions-file REF/ALT. Watch strand: PharmCAT's positions file is plus-strand genomic, and so is 23andMe, so they agree — but classic star-allele literature notation for CYP2D6 (e.g. 2851C>T for rs16947) is MINUS-strand gene notation and will look inverted. Trust the positions file, not the paper.
(d) For the many positions the chip never assayed, write ./. (truthful) and accept that PharmCAT reports uncalled haplotypes. Using --missing-to-ref will produce cleaner-looking but partly fictitious calls — if you use it for a demo, surface that fact in the UI.
(e) For CYP2D6, do not call from the array at all. Supply an outside call via `-po` with a tab-delimited file: column 1 HGNC gene symbol, column 2 diplotype, optional column 3 phenotype, optional column 4 activity score. Example line: `CYP2D6\t*1/*1`. PharmCAT marks these with callSource=OUTSIDE, which your adapter should display differently from MATCHER calls.
(f) bcftools has a `convert --tsv2vcf` path for 23andMe, but it still requires a GRCh38-aligned reference and does not solve the coverage problem.

demoPatientGenes.activityScore: null — CPIC does not use an activity score system for CYP2C19; PharmCAT emits Diplotype.activityScore = null and drives the lookup off the phenotype string. Do not fabricate a number here.
demoPatientGenes.typicalMissingPositions: *2 itself is well covered: rs4244285 (chr10:94781859 G>A, GRCh38, c.681G>A, p.Pro227=) is on 23andMe v3/v4/v5, as are rs4986893 (*3, chr10:94780653 G>A) and rs12248560 (*17, chr10:94761900 C>T). What a consumer array misses is the long tail of no-function alleles — *4, *5, *6, *7, *8, *35 and the rarer definitions. Consequence: an array-derived *1 is really 'no tested variant found', so a true *2/*4 poor metabolizer can be misreported as *1/*2 intermediate. PharmCAT surfaces this honestly in GeneReport.uncalledHaplotypes.

demoPatientGenes.activityScore: 2.0 (CPIC activity value of *1 is 1.0 per allele; 1.0 + 1.0 = 2.0, which falls in the CPIC normal-metabolizer band of 1.25–2.25). PharmCAT emits this as the STRING "2.0" in Diplotype.activityScore, with Haplotype.activityValue = "1.0" on each allele.
demoPatientGenes.typicalMissingPositions: This is the honest gap and the prototype should say so. PharmCAT explicitly recommends AGAINST calling CYP2D6 from VCF because structural and copy-number variation dominate the phenotype and are invisible to SNP/INDEL data. A consumer array typically does carry rs3892097 (*4, chr22:42128945 C>T) and rs1065852 (*10/*4-defining, chr22:42130692 G>A), and often rs16947 (chr22:42127941 G>A) and rs1135840 (chr22:42126611 C>G). It typically CANNOT see: gene duplications/multiplications (so ultrarapid metabolizers are missed entirely), whole-gene deletion *5 (which makes a hemizygous variant look homozygous), CYP2D6-CYP2D7 hybrid alleles, and indels such as rs5030655 (*6, chr22:42129083 CA>C). So an array-derived '*1/*1' means only 'no tested variant found' and cannot exclude UM or a hybrid. For the fixture, inject CYP2D6 as an OUTSIDE call (-po, line: CYP2D6<TAB>*1/*1) so callSource=OUTSIDE and the provenance is visible.

demoPatientGenes.activityScore: 2.0 — *2 is a normal-function allele with CPIC activity value 1.0, same as *1.
demoPatientGenes.typicalMissingPositions: Use this variant of the fixture if you want a non-reference diplotype that still yields NM. *2 is defined by rs16947 (chr22:42127941 G>A; classic notation 2851C>T p.Arg296Cys, minus-strand) together with rs1135840 (chr22:42126611 C>G; 4181G>C p.Ser486Thr). Both are commonly on consumer chips, but calling *2 correctly still requires phase and full allele-definition coverage, and the CNV blind spot is unchanged. All GRCh38 coordinates here were read directly out of PharmCAT's shipped pharmcat_positions.vcf.

notes:
CONFIDENCE AND PROVENANCE
Everything in pharmcatOutputShape was read from the actual Java source on the `development` branch of github.com/PharmGKB/PharmCAT — I grepped the @Expose/@SerializedName annotations rather than inferring from example output, so the key names are exact. All GRCh38 coordinates in demoPatientGenes were taken from PharmCAT's own `pharmcat_positions.vcf`, which is the same file PharmCAT matches against — so they cannot drift from what the tool expects.

GAPS AND THINGS I DID NOT CONFIRM (flagging rather than guessing):
1. I did NOT enumerate the serialized fields of MessageAnnotation, DrugLink, Publication, Genotype, or Metadata. If your adapter needs those, read the corresponding classes under reporter/model/.
2. The long-form spelling of the `-po` outside-call flag under pharmcat_pipeline is unconfirmed. Verify with `--help` before wiring it.
3. The `-research` mode flag value for CYP2D6-from-VCF (something like `-research cyp2d6`) is referenced in the docs but the exact token was not stated on the page I read. Confirm before use — and note PharmCAT actively discourages this mode.
4. `pharmcat_positions.vcf` on the development branch carries `##fileDate=2023-02-03`, but the file is re-cut per release. Pin the positions file to the same version as the Docker image or your fixture will silently drift.
5. CPIC's CYP2D6 phenotype bands have changed over time (the *10 activity value was downgraded 0.5 -> 0.25, and activity score 1.0 was reclassified from normal to intermediate metabolizer). My fixture avoids that boundary entirely — AS 2.0 is unambiguously NM under both old and current rules — but any lookup table you build MUST record which CPIC phenotype version it encodes. PharmCAT gives you this as GeneReport.phenotypeVersion; store it alongside every row.

ARCHITECTURAL NOTES FOR THE SWAP-READY ADAPTER
- Parse the REPORTER json (`-reporterJson`), not the phenotyper json, if you want drug recommendations — the phenotyper output has no drug layer at all. Read the phenotyper json only if you want calls without recommendations.
- The two top-level gene maps are named differently between artifacts (`geneReports` in phenotype.json vs `genes` in report.json) despite holding the same type. Normalize this at the adapter boundary or it will bite you.
- Model `activityScore` as `string | null` in TypeScript, not `number`. Parse to number only at the presentation layer, and preserve the original string for citation fidelity ("2.0" vs "2").
- `phenotypes` is an array and `lookupKey` is an array; do not assume singletons.
- Compute `missing` yourself from `VariantReport.call` being blank — there is no boolean for it.
- Because your architecture forbids the LLM inventing clinical facts: the fields that are safe to render verbatim as clinical content are AnnotationReport.drugRecommendation, .implications, .classification, .population, and GuidelineReport.url/DrugReport.citations for the citation. Everything else is metadata. Never let the model paraphrase drugRecommendation — pass it through.
- Keep the guideline-source discriminator (CPIC_GUIDELINE / DPWG_GUIDELINE / FDA_LABEL / FDA_ASSOC) all the way to the UI. CPIC and DPWG genuinely disagree on some antidepressant recommendations, and collapsing them would misrepresent both.

SCOPE CAVEAT WORTH STATING IN THE PROTOTYPE
A 23andMe-derived call is not a clinical result: wrong build, sparse coverage, no CNV, and no CLIA/CAP chain of custody. The conversion path above is good enough for a demo fixture and for exercising the adapter, but the prototype should display provenance (callSource, uncalledHaplotypes, missing-position count) rather than presenting array-derived diplotypes as equivalent to clinical genotyping. That is a UI requirement, not just a disclaimer.
